key_insight: ASCENT reveals a gap between answering complete medical questions and updating diagnostic impressions as information arrives, while targeted fine-tuning improves stepwise performance.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark evaluates reasoning closer to sequential clinical workflows, but its results do not establish safety or effectiveness in patient care.
method: Build 3,078 clinician-annotated stepwise problems from MedQA-USMLE.
Organize each vignette into EMR-aligned findings, impressions, and supporting rationales.
Evaluate LLMs, fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B and 32B, and test robustness and error propagation.
evidence_signal: ASCENT fine-tuning improved F1 over pre-trained and HuatuoGPT-o1 CoT-trained baselines, primarily through precision gains; the abstract does not report effect sizes.
watch_item: Errors can propagate across sequential predictions, and evaluation on exam-derived vignettes does not establish real-world clinical reliability.
paper_title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
